ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g1.finding: Long concrete entry steps are weathered and stained
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g1.matching_note: Weathered/stained concrete entry steps are clearly visible (dirt-darkened tread faces, stained nosings) but no condition on this photo covers the stairs at all. The only two conditions are the soffit/porch-ceiling degradation and the porch/facade curb-appeal modernization; neither one's observations touch the stair run, so I do not record curb_appeal_upgrade as a covering rejected condition here. The v5 catalog carries exterior degradation/wear items, so a weathered-hardscape surface is in principle billable -- hence miss_candidate rather than out_of_catalog, with the caveat that if the catalog treats generic concrete weathering as support-only wear this would flip to out_of_catalog.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g3.finding: Front porch and window openings have prominent metal security bars or grilles
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g3.matching_note: A black security grille over the porch-bay window and iron guard/bars at the porch opening are prominent in the image. No accepted condition covers them. I deliberately do NOT record curb_appeal_upgrade as covering: that condition was built only from 'The front porch looks dated' and 'The porch guard and ironwork feel dated', and the security-bar observation was severed from it when its own 2b bullet was dropped at 2c -- so the bar/grille observation was not in fact carried by any condition. Security-bar removal is a routine rehab scope item, so I treat it as catalog-capable; medium confidence on that point.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g4.finding: Corrugated downspout extension terminates at grade close to the basement window and foundation
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g4.matching_note: The white corrugated downspout extension discharging at grade against the foundation beside the low basement window is unambiguous in the photo, and 2a flagged it as a real concern ('Ensure water is carried well away from the foundation'). No condition of any kind on this photo touches drainage. Downspout discharge at the foundation is a standard exterior/drainage catalog scope, so this is a genuine billable miss, not an out-of-catalog observation.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g6.matching_note: The white storm/security door with scrollwork insert is visibly dated, and 2a called the entry door and storm/security treatment 'clear modernization opportunities'. No accepted condition covers it. curb_appeal_upgrade's claim text nominally spans 'entry/porch/facade', but its two constituent observations are both porch-scoped and the door observation never reached it (the door bullet was dropped at 2c), so I do not record it as a covering rejected condition. An entry/storm-door modernization is catalog-capable, so miss_candidate.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g7.finding: Metal step handrail is older with worn paint
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_001_g7.matching_note: The single narrow black stair handrail is older with dull/worn paint. 2a saw it ('The single narrow metal rail and porch guard/ironwork feel dated; replacing or refinishing them'), but 2b split that one sentence into two bullets and only the porch-guard half kept the 'dated' modifier -- that half survived into curb_appeal_upgrade while the stair-rail half went out at 2c. So the pipeline's surviving condition is about the porch guard, not the step handrail, and I do not record curb_appeal_upgrade as covering. Note the adjacency though: had curb_appeal_upgrade been routed to work rather than no_action, a porch/facade ironwork refinish would plausibly have swept the rail in.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_002_g1.matching_note: Counters read as granite-look laminate with a rolled edge — basic/dated, as gold says. No accepted condition covers countertops and no rejected condition on this photo covers them either (the only listed condition is the flooring one). A dated/basic countertop modernization item is the sort of thing this v5 catalog plainly carries (it carries older_flooring_style and dated_lighting_fixtures), so this is billable-in-principle, hence a miss rather than out_of_catalog. Note the catalog inventory itself was not inspected (Read-only review), so the in-catalog judgement is by analogy.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_002_g3.finding: Large open upper-cabinet niche contains an exposed unfinished wood shelf or board
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_002_g3.matching_note: The open upper-cabinet bay on the right has a bare unfinished wood shelf board with a raw front edge — an incomplete/unfinished cabinetry condition, not just a styling choice. No accepted condition covers cabinetry on this photo, and no rejected condition is listed. A cabinet defect/repair item (missing door / unfinished cabinetry) is the kind of item the catalog carries, so miss_candidate rather than out_of_catalog; catalog contents were not directly inspected.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_002_g6.matching_note: Two basic flush dome fixtures are clearly present. The pipeline got all the way to a resolved item: 2c survivor cd47781a6d1735ab -> dated_lighting_fixtures (modernization). It is the one issue absent from p2e.kept_issue_ids and matches the single tier_optional_suppressed count. Per the brief, 2e suppression never costs a condition, so a condition was projected — but no accepted condition covering lighting appears in conditions_on_photo. Caveat recorded deliberately: the review-excluded oc1_f46cc039d3163f19 (appendix_misnamed, case rc_4cab6e7be02b) is not inspectable here, so if that condition turns out to be the lighting one and is accepted, this row is a matched, not a miss, and the proto case below is a duplicate of rc_4cab6e7be02b. On the evidence I can see, no accepted condition covers it.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_002_g8.finding: Faucet and sink fittings are older/basic
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_002_g8.matching_note: Basic chrome faucet and side fitting on a stainless drop-in sink, consistent with gold's 'older/basic'. No accepted or rejected condition on this photo touches plumbing fixtures. A dated/basic fixture modernization item is directly analogous to dated_lighting_fixtures, which this catalog carries, so miss_candidate; catalog contents not directly inspected.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_003_g4.finding: Old wood rear door is rough and weathered with gaps
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_003_g4.matching_note: The old weathered wood door in the rough opening at center-right is clearly visible with gaps around the frame, and no condition on this photo touches a door - the four conditions cover ceiling, walls, floor and unfinished-space only. Doors are a standard component family in a rehab catalog (v5 already carries per-surface items like ceiling, wall and flooring wear), so I judge this billable in principle rather than normal-for-context. Residual uncertainty: retrieval is scene-group scoped and this photo is scene_group 'utility', so a door item may not be reachable here at all; if so this would be out_of_catalog rather than a miss. No rejected condition covers it.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_004_g4.finding: Laminate countertop is worn/stained near the range
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_004_g4.matching_note: Countertop wear/damage is visible (chipped, delaminated front edge on the left foreground counter; dingy discoloration near the sink). No accepted condition asserts counter wear: outdated_kitchen_finishes (oc1_e5cb60caefeab1cc) is a modernization claim that the counters are dated laminate, which is a different observation about the same object -- and the pipeline itself treated them as two separate issues. The degradation issue existed (70f737d3dba9a8ff, 'Laminate countertops show visible wear.') and died before becoming a condition, so there is no covering rejected condition either. Attributed in Part 3.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_005_g3.finding: Ceiling has a basic exposed-bulb light holder
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_005_g3.matching_note: The photo clearly shows a plain, exposed-bulb ceiling fixture. No condition on this photo covers lighting: the three conditions on record are popcorn ceiling texture (accepted), dated overall decor (rejected as generic) and wall scuffs (Terra-unsupported). Treated as miss_candidate rather than out_of_catalog because the v5 catalog carries granular modernization items of exactly this type (popcorn_or_acoustic_ceiling_texture, dated_overall_decor_style) and 2a itself framed the fixture as an upgrade opportunity ('a better light fixture/fan would modernize it quickly'), so a lighting-modernization item is very likely available. That judgement is the main uncertainty here - if the v5 catalog has no light-fixture item, this is out_of_catalog and not a miss. Caveat: excluded_condition_ids contains oc1_f46cc039d3163f19 (lane appendix_misnamed) which is not reproduced in conditions_on_photo, so I cannot rule out that it is a misnamed lighting condition that would make this a match.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_005_g4.finding: Walls have minor scuffs, small holes, and applied decal stickers
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_005_g4.matching_note: Gold asserts minor scuffs, small holes and applied decal stickers. The photo supports both halves: decals (butterflies/sunflowers) on the wall beside the windows, and small dark marks / nail-hole-sized specks plus screwed-in mounting hardware on the right-hand wall near the nightstand and the 'Towels' rack. A condition existed for this - oc1_32bf8869e625ef1f (wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents) - but Terra rejected it as unsupported, reasoning that the visible shapes near the windows are decorative decals. Terra is right about that specific area but the rejection is scoped to 'the visible walls near the windows' and misses the marks and fastener holes on the right wall, so the finding ends up unbilled. Recorded as miss_candidate with the rejected condition as coverage.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_006_g6.finding: Floor tile grout is darkened or stained in places
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_006_g6.matching_note: Darkened/stained grout on the bath floor tile is a degradation the v5 catalog can carry (the catalog demonstrably bills staining as a degradation elsewhere, e.g. bath_fixtures_stained_or_worn, and flooring degradation items exist in v5). No condition on this photo touches the floor at all - the three conditions are vanity, tub fixtures and dated finishes - and there is no rejected condition covering it, so nothing rejected to cite. Unbilled.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_006_g7.finding: Ceiling above the window has broad, uneven discoloration
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_006_g7.matching_note: Broad uneven ceiling discoloration above the window is a standard billable degradation (ceiling/wall staining or moisture marking) and reads in the photo as more than lighting falloff. No condition on this photo covers the ceiling, and no rejected condition exists to cite. Unbilled.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g3.finding: Cords/wiring are strung across the ceiling (surface-run)
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g3.matching_note: Surface-run cords/wiring across the ceiling is confirmed (yellow cord across the right ceiling, black cables along the left ceiling and hanging by the furnace). Unlike the other basement-normal findings this one IS carried by the v5 catalog: the bullet 'Numerous wires are loose and exposed.' survived 2c and resolved to visible_electrical_risks (issue f345ef1e6e5c7b70, present in p2e.kept_issue_ids). Yet conditions_on_photo shows no accepted condition covering it and no rejected one either, so no accepted v5 condition carries this finding -> miss_candidate. No covering rejected condition is recorded in the record, hence null. Caveat for the reviewer: this is the known parked electrical-observations class (electrical trade is product_quarantined), so this miss may be policy-intended rather than a pipeline defect; and it is possible, though unlikely on naming grounds, that the skipped oc1_f46cc039d3163f19 is this condition.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g6.finding: Painted masonry walls show peeling paint and staining
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g6.matching_note: Painted masonry walls with peeling paint and staining is confirmed in the photo (patchy grey/brown discoloration and flaking near the base of both the left wall behind the sink and the right wall). This is a genuine surface defect rather than basement-normal fabric, and the v5 catalog demonstrably carries analogous surface-staining/deterioration defects for this property (water_stain_ceiling on the same photo). No accepted condition covers it and no rejected condition covering it appears in the record, so covering_rejected_condition_id is null. Attribution is developed in the proto case: 2a never actually observed the defect, it only advised looking for it.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_001_g6.finding: Cornice and upper trim show weathering and paint wear
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_001_g6.matching_note: Weathering and worn paint on the cornice/upper trim is a first-class exterior degradation defect, not a normal-for-context artifact, and it is the kind of surface-wear/coating-breakdown condition v5 does carry (the catalog's degradation family includes surface aging and coating breakdown, as the patio_or_porch_surface_wear claim text itself shows). No condition of any kind was produced for the cornice, accepted or rejected, so there is no covering rejected condition. Caveat on catalog coverage: I could not open the v5 catalog to name the exact exterior trim/paint item, so the 'could have carried it' half of this call is inferred from the catalog's demonstrated degradation vocabulary rather than verified against the item list.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_001_g7.finding: Entry transom and surrounding trim show dark staining and finish wear
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_001_g7.matching_note: Same family as g6 — staining and worn finish on the entry transom and its surrounding trim is a degradation-kind surface condition v5's vocabulary covers, and no condition was produced for it. Weakest of the gold findings on the pixels: part of the darkness above the door is recessed-entry shadow under the lantern, so a reviewer could reasonably downgrade this to cosmetic grime and reclassify it out_of_catalog. Recording it as a miss_candidate because gold is photo-observation truth for this photo and the defect class is billable; the note is here so the call can be flipped without re-reading the image. Catalog-coverage caveat identical to g6 (item list not readable from this record).

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_002_g4.finding: Kitchen beyond has an older basic range and refrigerator
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_002_g4.matching_note: Older basic range and refrigerator are plainly visible through the opening and are ordinary modernization material for a rehab catalog with a modernization kind. No accepted condition on this photo covers appliances. No REJECTED covering condition can be named: the three listed conditions are all accepted, and any condition projected from the unresolved kitchen issue would sit in excluded_condition_ids, which I am instructed to skip. Caveat recorded in the proto case: the property's own kitchen photos may carry an accepted dated-kitchen condition, which would make this a photo-level miss but not a property-level one.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_002_g5.finding: Kitchen cabinetry visible beyond is minimal and dated

Treated as a separate finding from g4 because gold separates appliances from cabinetry, even though both trace to the single compound 2b bullet.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_002_g8.finding: Baseboards and door trim are scuffed with paint wear
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_002_g8.matching_note: Trim/door-casing paint wear is a distinct degradation the pipeline itself isolated ('Trim appears rough.', issue 9c707542dbbe52ea, kind degradation) and then failed to resolve to any catalog item. I do not treat it as covered by the accepted paint condition, because that condition's observation and terra rationale are anchored on ceiling/walls/openings, and because the pipeline kept trim as its own issue. Lower confidence than g4/g5: I could not verify offline that a trim/baseboard degradation item exists in the v5 catalog at run time (catalog 3.1 era); if none exists this is out_of_catalog rather than a miss.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_003_g2.finding: Window frames and sills show peeling paint and wear
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_003_g2.matching_note: Window frames/sills show chipped, peeling paint and a deteriorated left jamb in the photo. The pipeline generated a dedicated issue for this ('Window trim and sills show wear', issue 526c2fe305ccc860, kind degradation) which survived 2c and was kept at 2e, but 2d returned catalog_item_id null, so no condition was ever produced for window trim/sills. No rejected condition covers it. Partial-coverage caveat: the accepted room-level peeling_or_discolored_paint condition (oc1_65a72db32684dcd1) would in practice absorb trim repaint scope, so a reviewer may score this a partial rather than a full miss; the sill/trim wear itself is unbilled either way.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_003_g5.finding: Loose cable wiring is coiled on the floor and surface-run along the wall
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_003_g5.matching_note: The coiled black cable on the floor and the surface-run cable across the wall are clearly visible. The v5 catalog can carry this — 2d resolved the bullet to visible_electrical_risks (defect) — but no condition of that item appears anywhere in conditions_on_photo, accepted or rejected, so nothing reached Terra. Worth flagging that this may be intended behavior under the electrical product quarantine rather than a defect in the reader; recorded as a miss because the catalog item exists and the observation is real.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_003_g8.matching_note: The dated 4-blade fan is clearly visible and the pipeline read it correctly end to end: bullet 'The ceiling fan is dated.' survived 2c and 2d resolved older_ceiling_fan_style (modernization). ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g3.finding: Free-standing electric range is older and worn
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g3.matching_note: The older worn free-standing electric range is billed by nothing: no condition in conditions_on_photo references an appliance, accepted or rejected. 2a saw it ('older cabinetry, laminate counters, freestanding electric range' listed under 'Very dated kitchen'), 2b flattened it to the neutral inventory bullet 'The kitchen has a freestanding electric range.' with the dated quality stripped, and 2c then dropped that bullet. Caveat on the decision itself: I cannot confirm from this record that the v5 catalog carries an appliance item - every catalog id visible here is a fabric/finish/structure item (cabinets, counters, flooring, drywall, windows, doors, lighting). ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g7.finding: Window has bent/damaged blinds and plastic sheeting remnants; valance is dated
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g7.matching_note: The window area is unbilled. dated_or_older_windows exists as a condition on this photo, Terra SUPPORTED it ('older-style frame and blinds'), yet accepted=false with disposition no_action / reason_code route_no_action. The photo backs it up and then some: bent blinds, plastic sheeting remnants still taped at the jambs (a winterizing tell that supports the 'drafty' reading in 2a), dated valance. ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g8.finding: Round ceiling light fixture is dated
ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g8.matching_note: The dated round flush-mount ceiling fixture is unbilled, and unlike the window there is no covering condition to point at. ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g3.finding: Cords/wiring are strung across the ceiling (surface-run)

No covering rejected condition is recorded in the record, hence null. Caveat for the reviewer: this is the known parked electrical-observations class (electrical trade is product_quarantined), so this miss may be policy-intended rather than a pipeline defect; and it is possible, though unlikely on naming grounds, that the skipped oc1_f46cc039d3163f19 is this condition.

ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g6.finding: Painted masonry walls show peeling paint and staining
ga_redfin_10806500_photo_007_g6.matching_note: Painted masonry walls with peeling paint and staining is confirmed in the photo (patchy grey/brown discoloration and flaking near the base of both the left wall behind the sink and the right wall). ga_redfin_11000447_photo_001_g6.finding: Cornice and upper trim show weathering and paint wear

Caveat on catalog coverage: I could not open the v5 catalog to name the exact exterior trim/paint item, so the 'could have carried it' half of this call is inferred from the catalog's demonstrated degradation vocabulary rather than verified against the item list.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_001_g7.finding: Entry transom and surrounding trim show dark staining and finish wear

Weakest of the gold findings on the pixels: part of the darkness above the door is recessed-entry shadow under the lantern, so a reviewer could reasonably downgrade this to cosmetic grime and reclassify it out_of_catalog. Recording it as a miss_candidate because gold is photo-observation truth for this photo and the defect class is billable; the note is here so the call can be flipped without re-reading the image. Catalog-coverage caveat identical to g6 (item list not readable from this record).

No REJECTED covering condition can be named: the three listed conditions are all accepted, and any condition projected from the unresolved kitchen issue would sit in excluded_condition_ids, which I am instructed to skip. Partial-coverage caveat: the accepted room-level peeling_or_discolored_paint condition (oc1_65a72db32684dcd1) would in practice absorb trim repaint scope, so a reviewer may score this a partial rather than a full miss; the sill/trim wear itself is unbilled either way.

Worth flagging that this may be intended behavior under the electrical product quarantine rather than a defect in the reader; recorded as a miss because the catalog item exists and the observation is real.

ga_redfin_11000447_photo_003_g8.matching_note: The dated 4-blade fan is clearly visible and the pipeline read it correctly end to end: bullet 'The ceiling fan is dated.' survived 2c and 2d resolved older_ceiling_fan_style (modernization). ga_redfin_11000447_photo_004_g3.finding: Free-standing electric range is older and worn

Caveat on the decision itself: I cannot confirm from this record that the v5 catalog carries an appliance item - every catalog id visible here is a fabric/finish/structure item (cabinets, counters, flooring, drywall, windows, doors, lighting).
